resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §16 (forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose) line 55: scope: The rule is quoted correctly, but the finding fails on scope lens (c) and on its own harm claim.

1. A dated maintainer decision already covers this exact pattern. `curriculum/module-design/apt101-build-plan.md` § *Prompt convention* records the maintainer brief of 2026-10-07: "exercises can be built without expanding the prompts … reuse very much from a101". It then sets the rule: "Reused Agents 101 prompt → `{{prompt:<key>}}`, unchanged … **Never edit an Agents 101 prompt to fit; frame it in the exercise prose instead**." The digest steer and the door/full-path steer around `personal-agent-homework-2` are that sanctioned prose framing. The file's maintainer block (L112, *Reuse*) records it ("Framing in prose: the three-job menu in `-2` is steered to a digest"). It also points to the planned prompt-body pass where the A101 paths and bodies get reworked. The judge's main fix (put the steer inside the `personal-agent-homework-2` fence) breaks the maintainer's explicit "never edit an A101 prompt to fit". Its other fix (a new follow-up fence) is the "body-ask → new registry prompt" escalation that §16 Boundary 2 says needs maintainer sign-off. The decision is already made and dated. It sits in the build plan rather than as a §16-labelled note in the file, but that is a filing difference, not an open question.

2. The silent-failure harm is wrong. The full-path sentence only applies to text the prose itself adds: "Wherever `morning.md` names the door or the bet". The fence `personal-agent-homework-2` (checked) asks for a job, an output shape and "at least one hard boundary". It never mentions `team/`, the door or the bet. So a seat that pastes the fence without reading the paragraph gets a `morning.md` with no `team/` reference at all. There is no unresolvable path for the unattended run to trip on. The full-path instruction guards the prose's own door steer; it is not separate machinery that fails when skipped. Also, in the Code runtime `team/` is a link inside the training folder (`apt101-paint-the-product-box` L23, `apt101-d1-link-the-team-folder`), so relative paths resolve there anyway.

3. The prompt-only check (§16's diagnostic) passes for what carries the mood and the artefact. The beat's thread (Day 1 look-for line → Day 2 agreement) is fenced in `apt101-d1-your-look-for-line`, whose registry body writes `## Look for` into `morning.md` word for word. The expect line is fenced too (`apt101-d1-your-expect-line`). `morning.md` and `latest.html` land prompt-only through `personal-agent-homework-2` and `-3`. A missing door boundary is not silent either. Day 2 `apt101-read-the-digest` phase 1 (L33) checks for exactly this and names "the door in `team/what-goes-in.md`, or your brief" as what let a file through. A brief that left the door out becomes the lesson, not a broken opener.

Claims I verified as true: `-2` comes from A101 (`origin: exercises/personal-agent-homework`) and has no digest, door or full-path wording. The file has no §16 Boundary 2 accept-note. The L112 Reuse note does record the steer. None of these makes the finding blocking, given point 1. / harm: The judge's facts about the fence check out. `curriculum/prompts/personal-agent-homework-2.md` comes from A101 (origin: exercises/personal-agent-homework). Its three jobs are "morning plan, daily risk scan, or next-move draft", and it carries no digest steer, no door and no full path. The harm claim still falls apart.

1. **The silent failure the harm rests on no longer exists.** Line 55's full-path sentence came in with 9650ccf7 (arc-read fixes, "full team-folder path for scheduled runs"; `git blame` attributes the line to 13a3f580). A later commit, 387b3be5 ("new team-folder link (team/ was unreachable as a bare relative path)"), added `apt101-d1-link-the-team-folder`. That prompt runs in `apt101-paint-the-product-box` L25 and makes `team/` a link to the shared folder inside the training folder, not a copy. The scheduled run already finds `module-2/morning-agent/morning.md`, `memory/` and `style.md` by relative path (`personal-agent-homework-3`), so it runs from the training folder. From there, `team/...` resolves through the link. A seat that pastes the fence and skips the paragraph gets `team/` paths in morning.md, and the unattended run resolves them. The "silent Day 2 opener failure" doesn't happen. If anything, the full-path sentence is a leftover belt-and-braces from before the link existed. A fence that encodes it would be fixing a solved problem.

2. **The digest steer is a recorded design choice, and nothing downstream depends on it.** The maintainer block's Reuse note (L112) says the three-job menu in `-2` is steered to a digest in prose, which keeps the A101 shared fence untouched. What Day 2 actually consumes is the `## Look for` line and `expect.md`. Both are written by their own fenced prompts (`apt101-d1-your-look-for-line`, `apt101-d1-your-expect-line`), and those prompts do pass the prompt-only read. Pick "risk scan" and the brief still carries the person's own look-for sentence, which is the thing the Day 2 turn rests on. The door boundary is fenced too: `-2` makes the student name a hard boundary, the door is an existing team artefact, and Day 2 tests it aloud. The leftover harm is tidiness, not a missing artefact.

3. **The fix costs more than the defect.** Changing `personal-agent-homework-2` changes a prompt shared with A101 (AE101/A101 blast radius). A new fence adds a prompt to a beat that already has five, and §16 Boundary 2 says do not escalate a body ask to a new registry prompt without maintainer sign-off. The judge reads the missing accept-note as a breach. But the Reuse note already records the prose-steer choice in the maintainer block, which is a §16 accept in substance even without the word "Boundary 2".

Net: the one part that would make this blocking (a fence-only seat getting an unresolvable morning.md) is contradicted by the team-folder link added in 387b3be5.
